correctness.rationale: The EF1 inequalities become 2x_v≥d_v for even degrees; component double-counting forces ceil(m_component/2) selected edges. Alternating an Euler tour attains the bound and any larger cardinality by moving edges. Neutral goods yield the exact parity-adjusted imbalance. For 2-regular graphs, optimal allocations correspond to maximum matchings, counted by 2/even cycle and length/odd cycle. Labeled cycle EGFs give the finite probability formula; Gamma and logarithmic singular transfer give the parity-specific constants. The executable checks passed 741 finite Eulerian cases and all 4,058 labeled simple 2-regular graphs on 3–8 vertices. Finite tests are corroboration only; general assertions have analytic proof.

value.rationale: This resolves a natural precise fairness-and-cardinality optimization question in a sparse-incidence restriction of a contemporary fixed-group fairness problem. It supplies a constructive exact obstruction, a sharp neutral-item budget, an exact count for cycle supports, and a non-obvious parity-logarithmic decay of balanced-EF1 probability in a natural random 2-regular model, not merely isolated toy computations.
